questions.question: Requirements development consists of which four major activities?

Architectural design, implementing features, performing maintenance, and releasing the product

questions.question: What is a product champion?
options: The developer who writes the most code and therefore decides which user needs will be implemented
A representative of a user class who speaks for that group and may make decisions on its behalf
A tester who is solely responsible for writing and executing every acceptance test for the product
A person who must personally approve every software change regardless of its requirements impact

reference.excerpt: Track the status of each requirement, including states such as proposed, approved, implemented, or verified, so you can monitor how each change request is moving through development.
reference.lecture: Has it been approved? Proposed, approved, or implemented, or verified? So the proposed request can be either one of these four. So tracking that also is important where it is right now. And also some quantitative measures should be taken in terms of change quality of the changes.

questions.question: What does requirements volatility measure?
options: The rate at which requirements are changing during the project, not a measure of system speed
The defect density found in source code, which measures implementation quality rather than change rate
The measured level of customer satisfaction, which is not the definition of requirements volatility
The volume of data stored by the product, which does not describe how frequently requirements change
questions.explanation: Volatility refers to how frequently or rapidly requirements change.

reference.excerpt: Requirements management includes measuring requirements volatility, the rate at which requirements are changing, along with the reasons those changes are occurring.
reference.lecture: Welcome to chapter 3. In this chapter, we look at the requirement engineering as we described in chapter 1 more in detail. If you recall that requirement engineering consists of requirements development and requirements management. So there are two parts, initial development and management.

questions.question: High requirements volatility can indicate which possible problems? Select all that apply.
options: A poor understanding of the real requirements, which can cause frequent corrections and churn
An ill-defined project scope, which leaves the boundary unstable and invites constant change
Changing business conditions that force the team to revise previously agreed requirements
Organizational or political issues that drive repeated changes unrelated to genuine product need
questions.explanation: The slides mention poor understanding, weak scope definition, business dynamics, and politics as possible causes of high volatility.

reference.excerpt: High change rates can indicate poor understanding of the requirements, an ill-defined project scope, changing business conditions, organizational or political issues, or instability in the requirements process.
reference.lecture: Welcome to chapter 3. In this chapter, we look at the requirement engineering as we described in chapter 1 more in detail. If you recall that requirement engineering consists of requirements development and requirements management. So there are two parts, initial development and management.

questions.question: Why might a requirements management tool be useful?
options: A tool removes the need for requirements analysts because the software can elicit needs by itself
A tool makes customer involvement unnecessary because stakeholders no longer need to review needs
A tool eliminates the need to write requirements because the repository invents them automatically
Automation can reduce repetitive work and support tracking, versioning, and traceability tasks
questions.explanation: The slides note that tools can eliminate drudgery and help perform requirements management tasks more effectively.

reference.excerpt: Commercial requirements management tools store requirements in a database and help implement and automate tracking, versioning, change history, and traceability tasks, reducing repetitive manual work.
reference.lecture: Welcome to chapter 3. In this chapter, we look at the requirement engineering as we described in chapter 1 more in detail. If you recall that requirement engineering consists of requirements development and requirements management. So there are two parts, initial development and management.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a requirements traceability matrix?
options: To store stakeholder contact lists rather than to link requirements to later development artifacts
To connect each requirement to the design, code, and tests that implement and verify that requirement
To calculate the project budget and staffing cost rather than to link requirements through artifacts
To track project budget line items, which is a cost-accounting concern rather than requirements tracing
questions.explanation: A traceability matrix links requirements through later development artifacts.

reference.excerpt: A requirements traceability matrix is a set of links that connect each functional requirement to the design and code elements that implement it and the tests that verify it.
reference.lecture: Welcome to chapter 3. In this chapter, we look at the requirement engineering as we described in chapter 1 more in detail. If you recall that requirement engineering consists of requirements development and requirements management. So there are two parts, initial development and management.

questions.question: Which benefits can a traceability matrix provide? Select all that apply.
options: Help ensure that required functionality is not missed during design, construction, and testing
Connect each requirement to the code and tests that implement and verify that requirement
Help prevent unwanted features from appearing when they have no approved requirement source
Support tracking of requirements as they move through development and later change activity
questions.explanation: Traceability helps ensure required work is implemented and prevents functionality with no requirement justification from being added.

reference.excerpt: A traceability matrix helps confirm that required functionality is implemented and verified, supports tracking through development, and helps stop developers from adding unauthorized features.
reference.lecture: Welcome to chapter 3. In this chapter, we look at the requirement engineering as we described in chapter 1 more in detail. If you recall that requirement engineering consists of requirements development and requirements management. So there are two parts, initial development and management.

questions.question: A developer adds a feature that cannot be traced back to any approved requirement. What problem can traceability help reveal?
options: A user-training gap, which is not what missing requirement-to-feature traces are meant to expose
An extraneous or unauthorized feature that was added without an approved requirement source
A database-indexing problem, which is a design-performance issue rather than a tracing finding
A requirements baseline that automatically fails, which is not the problem this scenario describes
questions.explanation: Traceability can expose features that were added without an approved requirement.

reference.excerpt: Traceability keeps requirements from being forgotten and stops developers from adding unauthorized features. A feature that cannot be traced to an approved requirement is extraneous.
reference.lecture: Welcome to chapter 3. In this chapter, we look at the requirement engineering as we described in chapter 1 more in detail. If you recall that requirement engineering consists of requirements development and requirements management. So there are two parts, initial development and management.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the overall Chapter 3 process?
options: Develop requirements iteratively through elicitation, analysis, specification, and validation, then manage changes in a controlled and traceable way
Write every requirement in a single linear pass, freeze that document so it cannot change, and only then allow the construction work to begin
Let customers define all technical design and architecture choices, skipping a disciplined requirements development and change-management process
Skip analysis and specification entirely and rely only on prototypes, without validating a reviewable requirements baseline for the product
questions.explanation: Chapter 3 presents requirements engineering as an iterative development process followed by disciplined requirements management.

reference.book: Chapter 3 — A requirements development process framework
reference.excerpt: Requirements development is iterative through elicitation, analysis, specification, and validation. Requirements management then deals with those requirements after you have them, using change control and tracing.
